messages:
incident-bot: FIRE: GPU autoscaler alerts for inference-prod (queue > 5k, 95p latency > 12s). Paging oncall-sre now. :rotating_light:

ana (oncall-sre): acked. I'm pulling up HPA and queue metrics, will update in 2 mins.

leo (runtime): flipping on my laptop, saw increase in queued requests around 08:42 UTC. Could be a rollout of the new bert-long config?

maya (support): we've got customer CS tickets about 503s and long waits for embeddings since ~08:45. Notifying affected accounts.

ana (oncall-sre): top-level check: kubectl get hpa -n prod inference-gpu
```
NAME               REFERENCE               TARGETS   MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS   AGE
inference-gpu      Deployment/inference    0%/80%    2         80        2          3d
```
Looks like desired replicas stuck at 2 even though queue is high. HPA metrics show 0/80% because custom metric not reporting.

ana (oncall-sre): checking metrics-server / adapter logs.

ops-bot: logs forwarded from metrics-adapter pod metrics-adapter-0:
```
E0518 08:46:11.123456 1 adapter.go:214] could not unmarshal sample: label value too long or high cardinality: "model_variant=bert-long-20260518-xyzt..."
E0518 08:46:11.123789 1 cache.go:88] dropping metric inference/queued_requests: failed to convert sample to metric
```

leo (runtime): that's new — we pushed a change earlier that added `model_variant` as a label on per-request metrics for debugging. Likely exploded cardinality.

ana (oncall-sre): confirmed Prometheus scrape shows sample rate drop for custom metric inference/queued_requests after 08:44. Adapter is rejecting samples with high-cardinality labels. That's why HPA doesn't see load.

maya (support): customer impact so far — estimated 13% of production requests started getting 503s, and median latency for others jumped from 0.7s -> 6s. Noting list of affected orgs, escalating to CS lead.

leo (runtime): mitigation plan: 1) remove high-card label from metrics emitter (revert) 2) restart adapter (to clear bad samples) 3) manual scale up GPU pool to absorb backlog 4) set HPA minReplicas=8 to prevent under-scaling while metrics catch up.

ana (oncall-sre): doing #4 now.
```
kubectl patch hpa inference-gpu -n prod --patch '{"spec":{"minReplicas":8}}'
```

ops-bot: HPA minReplicas patched -> 8 (requested by ana).

sre-night: oncall handoff scheduled at 09:15 UTC. I'm joining the thread for the handoff window.

leo (runtime): rolling back emitter change to remove `model_variant` label and redeploying emitter service.
```
# git revert HEAD
kubectl rollout restart deployment/metric-emitter -n prod
```

ops-bot: metric-emitter rollout started.

ana (oncall-sre): restarting metrics-adapter to force re-sync with Prometheus.
```
kubectl rollout restart deployment/metrics-adapter -n kube-system
kubectl logs deployment/metrics-adapter -n kube-system --since=5m | tail -n 50
```

ops-bot: metrics-adapter restart completed, logs show adapter started and registered custom metrics.

ana (oncall-sre): checking Prometheus / adapter: inference/queued_requests now visible and aggregated. HPA shows desired count climbing.

kubectl get hpa -n prod inference-gpu
```
NAME               REFERENCE               TARGETS       MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS   AGE
inference-gpu      Deployment/inference    1200/80%      8         80        12         4h
```
(12 replicas coming up)

leo (runtime): also asked platform to open burst capacity; kevin, can you spin up two extra GPU nodes for immediate capacity?

kevin (platform): ACK, provisioning 2x V100 nodes with fast path. ETA ~6 minutes.

maya (support): CS notified affected customers about mitigation steps and ETA. Will follow up with root cause once we have it.

ana (oncall-sre): manual queue drain observed — queued_requests metric declining from 5400 -> 900 over 18 minutes. Error rate dropping.

ops-bot: autoscaler events:
```
Normal scaled from 2 to 8 (min bump)
Normal scaled from 8 to 12 (HPA desired)
```

sre-night: taking 09:15-10:15 UTC on-call. ana handing over: emitter revert + adapter restart done, HPA min bumped, platform scaled nodes, CS notified. No ongoing customer escalations pending.

ana (oncall-sre): handing off. Notes: root cause appears to be high-cardinality label (`model_variant`) introduced in metric-emitter which caused metrics-adapter to drop custom metric samples. That prevented HPA from seeing queue pressure. Secondary issue: emitter rollout coincided with peak traffic -> exacerbated.

leo (runtime): followups I'm owning: 1) revert is in prod (monitoring for any regressions) 2) sanitize metrics: strip per-request high-card labels, add sampled variant tag if needed 3) add unit test and a CI gate to reject new public metric labels with >10 cardinality estimated.

kevin (platform): followups: 1) investigate quota on metrics-adapter and improve throttling/error visibility 2) consider fallback HPA policy: if custom metric missing for >2m, use queue length from Redis as fallback 3) evaluate burst GPU pool auto-provisioning thresholds.

maya (support): CS action items: confirm SLA impact window, draft customer postmortem note.

ana (oncall-sre): incident severity: SEV2 (partial outage for multi-tenant inference; degraded for ~22 minutes until manual mitigations scaled capacity, full recovery by 09:05 UTC).

ops-bot: incident timeline appended to incident tracker.

sre-night: I'll keep watch and will escalate to infra team if queued_requests trend reverses.

leo (runtime): logging followup: here's the problematic log pattern from metric-emitter before revert:
```
INFO 08:44:05 Emit metric queued_requests{model_variant="bert-long-20260518-xyzt123abcd"} 1
INFO 08:44:06 Emit metric queued_requests{model_variant="bert-long-20260518-qwerty987"} 1
```
That equals many unique label values per request.

ana (oncall-sre): postmortem action items summarized in ticket INF-4532:
- Runtime: add label cardinality guardrails and CI check (owner: leo)
- Platform: HPA fallback metric + better adapter monitoring (owner: kevin)
- SRE: runbook update for manual HPA bump + immediate adapter restart (owner: ana)
- Support: customer communication template + notify impacted accounts (owner: maya)

maya (support): copying CS lead on the ticket and will sync tomorrow at 11:00 PT.

kevin (platform): provisioning nodes completed, cluster autoscaler metrics look healthy now.

sre-night: monitoring for 1h, setting follow-up review for tomorrow. Good work everyone. :thumbsup:

ana (oncall-sre): closing my shift, leaving thread with current snapshot and links to logs/dashboards.

incident-bot: incident closed (mitigated) by ana at 09:05 UTC, follow-up review scheduled.
